html:
The Pomo are a Native American people of Northern California, whose lands ran from the Pacific coast inland to Clear Lake, north of San Francisco Bay.

They were not one tribe but many small village communities speaking seven related but distinct Pomoan languages. Their neighbours included the Wappo, the Patwin and the Miwok. They lived on acorns, fish, game and seeds, and traded beads made of clamshell and red magnesite, which served as money across the region.

Pomo women made some of the finest baskets in the world, tightly woven and often covered in feathers and shell.

In 1812 the Russians built Fort Ross on Kashaya Pomo land. Spanish and Mexican ranchers took Pomo labour in the 1830s and 1840s. During the Gold Rush years, US soldiers killed many Pomo at Clear Lake in the Bloody Island massacre of 1850. Today the Pomo belong to many small rancherias and tribes.
sum: The Pomo are a Native American people of Northern California, whose lands ran from the Pacific coast inland to Clear Lake, north of San Francisco Bay.
